subproblem.title: Hausdorff measure on the span of an orthonormal n-frame is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P (Euclid P). Put ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i (s_i the coordinates of s ∈ ℝ^n = Euclid n), and Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. Then the n-dimensional Euclidean Hausdorff measure H^n = μHE[n] restricted to Q is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure L^n (volume on ℝ^n) under ι: H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n), i.e. μHE[n].restrict Q = Measure.map ι volume.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (μHE[n] : Measure (Euclid P)).restrict (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) = Measure.map (fun s : Euclid n => ∑ i, s i • τ i) volume
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent-supplied proof ("H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n) (μHE[n] is preserved by isometries and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n; Mathlib Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image, EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume)"), stated as a separate lemma because the transfer between the plane Q and the parameter space ℝ^n is used repeatedly in the sibling plane_constancy_reduction. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; L^n := volume on ℝ^n = Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); s_i are the coordinates of s ∈ ℝ^n; ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i; Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. Nothing is assumed about n or P beyond τ being orthonormal (n = 0 is allowed: then Q = {0} and ι is the map from the one-point space ℝ^0 to 0).
1. (ι is a linear isometry.) ι is linear (ι(s + t) = ι(s) + ι(t), ι(cs) = cι(s)). For s ∈ ℝ^n, orthonormality gives ⟨ι(s), ι(s)⟩ = Σ_{i,k} s_i s_k ⟨τ_i, τ_k⟩ = Σ_i s_i² = ‖s‖² (Mathlib Orthonormal.inner_sum together with the Euclidean norm formula EuclideanSpace.norm_eq). Hence ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖ for all s, and, ι being additive, ‖ι(s) − ι(t)‖ = ‖ι(s − t)‖ = ‖s − t‖: ι is an isometry (AddMonoidHomClass.isometry_of_norm).
2. (range ι = Q.) Each ι(s) = Σ_i s_i τ_i is a linear combination of τ_1, …, τ_n, hence lies in Q. Conversely, every y ∈ Q = span{τ_1, …, τ_n} can be written y = Σ_i c_i τ_i with c : Fin n → ℝ (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun), i.e. y = ι(c) where c is regarded as the element of ℝ^n with coordinates c_i. So range ι = Q.
3. (Isometry invariance of μHE[n].) For an isometry f : X → Y between metric spaces carrying their Borel σ-algebras, the push-forward of μHE[d] under f is μHE[d] restricted to the range of f: (μHE[d]).map f = μHE[d].restrict (range f) (Mathlib Isometry.map_euclideanHausdorffMeasure; it expresses H^d(f(A)) = H^d(A), the isometry invariance of Hausdorff measure, together with the fact that f is a measurable embedding with image range f). Applying it to ι (step 1) with d = n and using step 2: (μHE[n] on ℝ^n).map ι = μHE[n].restrict (range ι) = μHE[n].restrict Q.
4. (Normalization.) On ℝ^n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) the measure μHE[n] equals Lebesgue measure: μHE[n] = volume (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume; the normalizing factor in the definition of μHE[n] is chosen exactly so that this holds).
5. (Conclusion.) Substituting 4 into 3: μHE[n].restrict Q = volume.map ι = Measure.map ι volume, i.e. H^n⌞Q = ι_#(L^n). ∎

subproblem.title: Extension of a test function on the parameter domain of a plane to an ambient test function
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i, and Ω := {s ∈ ℝ^n : ι(s) ∈ V}. Let ψ : ℝ^n → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ Ω. Then there is a C^∞ function f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V such that, for every s ∈ ℝ^n, f(ι(s)) = ψ(s) and Df(ι(s))(τ_j) = Dψ(s)(e_j) for every j, where e_j = EuclideanSpace.single j 1 is the j-th standard basis vector of ℝ^n and Df(y)(v) = fderiv ℝ f y v.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P) (ψ : Euclid n → ℝ), IsOpen V → Orthonormal ℝ τ → ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) ψ → HasCompactSupport ψ → tsupport ψ ⊆ {s : Euclid n | ∑ i, s i • τ i ∈ V} → ∃ f : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f ∧ HasCompactSupport f ∧ tsupport f ⊆ V ∧ ∀ s : Euclid n, f (∑ i, s i • τ i) = ψ s ∧ ∀ j : Fin n, fderiv ℝ f (∑ i, s i • τ i) (τ j) = fderiv ℝ ψ s (EuclideanSpace.single j (1 : ℝ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent-supplied proof, construction of the ambient test function: "Since ι(spt ψ) is a compact subset of the open set V, there is δ > 0 with {y ∈ ℝ^P : ι^*(y) ∈ spt ψ, |y − p_Q(y)| ≤ δ} ⊆ V, where ι^*(y) := (⟨y, τ_1⟩, …, ⟨y, τ_n⟩) and p_Q is the orthogonal projection onto Q. With χ ∈ C^∞_c(ℝ^P), χ = 1 near 0, spt χ ⊆ B_δ(0), put f(y) := ψ(ι^*(y))·χ(y − p_Q(y)): f ∈ C^∞_c(V), f(ι(s)) = ψ(s) and D_{τ_i}f(ι(s)) = ∂_iψ(s)". Notation: ‖·‖ is the Euclidean norm; B(0, ρ), B̄(0, ρ) are open and closed balls; cthickening δ A := {y : inf_{a∈A}‖y − a‖ ≤ δ}.
1. (Linear maps.) ι is linear and ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖ (orthonormality: ‖Σ s_iτ_i‖² = Σ s_i²). Let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^n, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_1, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_n, y⟩), a continuous linear map; let p := ι∘ι* (the orthogonal projection onto Q = span{τ_i}) and q := id − p, both continuous linear. By orthonormality, ι*(ι(s)) = s (⟨τ_k, Σ_i s_iτ_i⟩ = s_k) and ι*(τ_j) = e_j; consequently q(ι(s)) = ι(s) − ι(ι*(ι(s))) = 0, and every y satisfies y = p(y) + q(y) with ‖p(y)‖ = ‖ι*(y)‖.
2. (Margin.) K := tsupport ψ is compact (ψ has compact support) and K ⊆ Ω, so ι(K) is compact (ι continuous) and ι(K) ⊆ V. Since V is open, there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ (ι(K)) ⊆ V (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open). Let R ≥ 0 with K ⊆ B̄(0, R) (K is bounded).
3. (Cutoff.) Let χ : ℝ^P → ℝ be a smooth bump function centred at 0 with inner radius δ/2 and outer radius δ (Mathlib ContDiffBump with rIn = δ/2 < rOut = δ): χ is C^∞, χ = 1 on B̄(0, δ/2) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall), and the support of χ is B(0, δ) (ContDiffBump.support_eq).
4. (Definition.) f(y) := ψ(ι*(y))·χ(q(y)). f is C^∞: ψ∘ι* and χ∘q are compositions of C^∞ functions with continuous linear maps, and products of C^∞ functions are C^∞.
5. (Support.) If f(y) ≠ 0 then ψ(ι*(y)) ≠ 0, so ι*(y) ∈ K, and χ(q(y)) ≠ 0, so ‖q(y)‖ < δ. Hence support f ⊆ A := {y : ι*(y) ∈ K and ‖q(y)‖ ≤ δ}. A is closed (K is closed; ι*, q and the norm are continuous), so tsupport f ⊆ A. A is bounded: for y ∈ A, ‖y‖ ≤ ‖p(y)‖ + ‖q(y)‖ = ‖ι*(y)‖ + ‖q(y)‖ ≤ R + δ. So A is compact (closed and bounded in ℝ^P) and f has compact support (HasCompactSupport.of_support_subset_isCompact). For y ∈ A, p(y) = ι(ι*(y)) ∈ ι(K) and ‖y − p(y)‖ = ‖q(y)‖ ≤ δ, so y ∈ cthickening δ (ι(K)) ⊆ V. Hence tsupport f ⊆ A ⊆ V.
6. (Values on Q.) For s ∈ ℝ^n: ι*(ι(s)) = s and q(ι(s)) = 0, so f(ι(s)) = ψ(s)·χ(0) = ψ(s) (0 ∈ B̄(0, δ/2)).
7. (Derivatives on Q.) Fix s ∈ ℝ^n. Since q is continuous and q(ι(s)) = 0, the set N := {y : q(y) ∈ B̄(0, δ/2)} is a neighbourhood of ι(s), and on N, χ(q(y)) = 1, so f = ψ∘ι* on N. Functions that agree near a point have the same derivative there (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq), so by the chain rule Df(ι(s)) = D(ψ∘ι*)(ι(s)) = Dψ(ι*(ι(s)))∘ι* = Dψ(s)∘ι*. Therefore Df(ι(s))(τ_j) = Dψ(s)(ι*(τ_j)) = Dψ(s)(e_j) for every j (step 1). ∎

subproblem.title: Vanishing boundary gives the ambient weak-derivative identity ∫_{V∩Q} g·D_{τ_j}f dHⁿ = 0
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, V ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∈ 𝒟_n(V) with ∂S = 0 in V (BoundaryVanishes S), τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, and g : ℝ^P → ℝ such that S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) (H^n = μHE[n]). Then for every C^∞ function f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V, and every index j, ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·Df(x)(τ_j) dH^n(x) = 0, where Df(x)(v) = fderiv ℝ f x v.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P) (g : Euclid P → ℝ), 1 ≤ n → Orthonormal ℝ τ → BoundaryVanishes S → (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, S ω = ∫ x in V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), g x * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x τ ∂μHE[n]) → ∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) f → HasCompactSupport f → tsupport f ⊆ V → ∀ j : Fin n, ∫ x in V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), g x * fderiv ℝ f x (τ j) ∂μHE[n] = 0
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 6 ("Zero weak derivatives") of the parent-supplied proof, ambient part: "φ := f·α_i ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(V). Then dφ = df ∧ α_i and ⟨dφ(x), ξ_Q⟩ = (−1)^{i−1}D_{τ_i}f(x). Since ∂S = 0 in V, 0 = ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = (−1)^{i−1}∫_{V∩Q} g D_{τ_i}f dH^n"; Simon Ch. 6, proof of 2.34, formula (2) (d ω_j = (D_j a) dx^1 ∧ ⋯ ∧ dx^n). Here the sign (−1)^{i−1} is absorbed into the choice of the constant (n−1)-covector, so that dφ(x)(τ) = Df(x)(τ_j) exactly. Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; indices of τ run over Fin n = {0, …, n−1}; for a family w = (w_0, …, w_m), Fin.removeNth i w is the family with entry i deleted; α(τ) := α(τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}).
1. (Degree.) Since n ≥ 1, write n = m + 1. Then BoundaryVanishes S means S.boundary = 0, i.e. ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = 0 for every φ ∈ 𝒟^m(V) (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply: ∂S(φ) = S(dφ), where dφ = exteriorDerivative φ belongs to 𝒟^n(V) because d preserves smoothness and compact support and tsupport dφ ⊆ tsupport φ).
2. (A constant m-covector.) Let e_0, …, e_m be the standard basis of ℝ^{m+1}. By the accepted sibling coordinate_covector (dgcr_bwd_coordinate_covector) there is an m-covector β on ℝ^{m+1} with β(Fin.removeNth i e) = (−1)^j if i = j and = 0 if i ≠ j (explicitly β(w_1, …, w_m) = det[e_j, w_1, …, w_m]: if i ≠ j the family (e_j, Fin.removeNth i e) contains e_j twice; if i = j, moving e_j to position j costs j transpositions). Let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^{m+1}, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_0, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_m, y⟩), a continuous linear map; by orthonormality ι*(τ_k) = e_k. Define the m-covector α on ℝ^P by α(w_1, …, w_m) := β(ι*w_1, …, ι*w_m) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap). Then for every i, α(Fin.removeNth i τ) = β(Fin.removeNth i (ι*∘τ)) = β(Fin.removeNth i e) = (−1)^j if i = j, and 0 otherwise.
3. (Test form.) Let f be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V, and put φ(y) := f(y)·α (a constant covector times a scalar function). φ is C^∞, has compact support, and tsupport φ ⊆ tsupport f ⊆ V; so φ ∈ 𝒟^m(V).
4. (Exterior derivative.) For every x ∈ ℝ^P and every family w = (w_0, …, w_m), since f is differentiable at x and α is constant,
 dφ(x)(w) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·D[y ↦ f(y)α(Fin.removeNth i w)](x)(w_i) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i·Df(x)(w_i)·α(Fin.removeNth i w)
 (the alternating-sum formula for the exterior derivative, SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_apply in Chapter06/Forms.lean, dφ(x)(w) = Σ_i (−1)^i·D[y ↦ φ(y)(Fin.removeNth i w)](x)(w_i), applied to the form φ, which is differentiable at x; for each i the scalar function y ↦ φ(y)(Fin.removeNth i w) equals f(y)·c_i with the constant c_i := α(Fin.removeNth i w), whose derivative at x is c_i·Df(x) (fderiv_mul_const)). Taking w = τ and using step 2, only the term i = j survives: dφ(x)(τ) = (−1)^j·Df(x)(τ_j)·(−1)^j = Df(x)(τ_j).
5. (Conclusion.) By step 1 and the hypothesis on S applied to ω := dφ ∈ 𝒟^n(V):
 0 = ∂S(φ) = S(dφ) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·dφ(x)(τ) dH^n(x) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·Df(x)(τ_j) dH^n(x),
 the last equality because the two integrands agree at every point by step 4. ∎

subproblem.title: Carrier in an n-plane: the orientation is ±τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ almost everywhere
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (R : IMRep U n with M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient). Let τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) be an orthonormal family in ℝ^P and Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}. If H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0 (H^n = μHE[n]), then for H^n-a.e. x ∈ M (that is, μHE[n].restrict M-a.e.) either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n), or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))) = 0 → ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, R.orient x α = α τ) ∨ (∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, R.orient x α = -α τ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 ("Orientation") of the parent-supplied proof, which this child states separately; Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (approximate tangent space) and Ch. 6, 3.1 (orientation of an integer multiplicity current). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α (a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P) and a family σ = (σ_1, …, σ_n), α(σ) := α(σ_1, …, σ_n); η_{x,r}(y) := r^{−1}(y − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r); B(q, ρ) and B̄(q, ρ) are the open and closed balls.

subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n} with V ∩ Q connected, ι : ℝ^n → ℝ^P, ι(s) := Σ_i s_i τ_i, Ω := {s ∈ ℝ^n : ι(s) ∈ V}, H^n = μHE[n] and L^n = Lebesgue measure (volume) on ℝ^n. Let g : ℝ^P → ℝ satisfy: (i) g is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞Q; (ii) g(x) ∈ ℤ for H^n⌞Q-a.e. x; (iii) ∫_{K∩Q} |g| dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V (|g| = ‖g‖ₑ, lower integral); (iv) ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·Df(x)(τ_j) dH^n(x) = 0 for every C^∞ f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport f ⊆ V and every j. Put h := g∘ι. Then (a) Ω is open; (b) Ω is preconnected; (c) h is locally integrable on Ω with respect to L^n; (d) ∫_{ℝ^n} h(s)·Dφ(s)(e_i) ds = 0 for every C¹ function φ : ℝ^n → ℝ with compact support and tsupport φ ⊆ Ω and every i, where e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ i; (e) for every c₀ ∈ ℝ with h(s) = c₀ for L^n-a.e. s ∈ Ω there is c ∈ ℤ with g(x) = c for H^n-a.e. x ∈ V ∩ Q.

Source: steps 3, 6 (transfer to the parameter domain), 7 and the first half of 8 of the parent-supplied proof, except for the distributional constancy theorem itself: "Let Ω := ι^{−1}(V) ⊆ ℝ^n (open; ι restricts to a homeomorphism of Ω onto V ∩ Q, so Ω is connected and nonempty) and h := g∘ι ∈ L¹_loc(Ω) … 0 = ∂S(φ) = (−1)^{i−1}∫_Ω h(s)∂_iψ(s) ds by (3) and (5)"; "(If a library form of this fact tests against C¹_c functions, note that (6) extends from ψ ∈ C^∞_c(Ω) to ψ ∈ C¹_c(Ω) …) Since h takes integer values and h = c on a set of positive measure (Ω is open and nonempty), c ∈ ℤ"; "since ι maps L^n-null subsets of Ω onto H^n-null subsets of V ∩ Q (by (3)), g = c H^n-a.e. on V ∩ Q". 1. (Plane measure, supplied step 3.) By the sibling plane_measure_map (idtp_pc_plane_hausdorff_eq_map), H^n⌞Q = ι_#L^n. The map ι is an isometry (orthonormality: ‖ι(s)‖ = ‖s‖, ι linear), hence a closed embedding and therefore a measurable embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding, IsClosedEmbedding.measurableEmbedding). Consequently, for every measurable A ⊆ ℝ^P:
 (1a) H^n⌞(A ∩ Q) = (H^n⌞Q)⌞A = ι_#(L^n⌞ι^{−1}(A)) (Measure.restrict_restrict, MeasurableEmbedding.restrict_map);
 (1b) ∫_{A∩Q} F dH^n = ∫_{ι^{−1}(A)} F(ι(s)) ds for every F : ℝ^P → ℝ (Bochner; MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map) and the same for lower integrals of F : ℝ^P → [0, ∞] (MeasurableEmbedding.lintegral_map);
 (1c) a property holds for H^n⌞(A ∩ Q)-a.e. x iff it holds at ι(s) for L^n⌞ι^{−1}(A)-a.e. s (MeasurableEmbedding.ae_map_iff);

2. ((a) Ω is open.) Ω = ι^{−1}(V) with ι continuous and V open.
3. ((b) Ω is preconnected.) Let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^n, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_1, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_n, y⟩) (continuous). Every y ∈ Q has the form y = Σ_i c_iτ_i, and then ⟨τ_k, y⟩ = c_k, so y = ι(ι*(y)); also ι*(ι(s)) = s and ι(s) ∈ Q for all s. Hence ι*(V ∩ Q) = Ω: if y ∈ V ∩ Q then ι(ι*(y)) = y ∈ V, i.e. ι*(y) ∈ Ω; if s ∈ Ω then ι(s) ∈ V ∩ Q and ι*(ι(s)) = s. As V ∩ Q is connected and ι* is continuous, Ω = ι*(V ∩ Q) is connected (IsPreconnected.image), in particular preconnected and nonempty.
4. ((c) local integrability.) By (i) and (1d), h = g∘ι is a.e.-strongly measurable for L^n. Let K' ⊆ Ω be compact. Then ι(K') is compact with ι(K') ⊆ V, measurable (closed), and ι^{−1}(ι(K')) = K' (ι is injective). By (1b) with A := ι(K') and (iii): ∫_{K'} |h| dL^n = ∫_{ι(K')∩Q} |g| dH^n < ∞. So h is integrable on every compact subset of the open set Ω, i.e. locally integrable on Ω (locallyIntegrableOn_iff, Ω being open, hence locally closed).
5. (Smooth tests; supplied step 6, last equality.) Let ψ : ℝ^n → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport ψ ⊆ Ω, and let j be an index. By the sibling plane_test_extension (idtp_pc_plane_test_extension) there is a C^∞ f : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support, tsupport f ⊆ V and Df(ι(s))(τ_j) = Dψ(s)(e_j) for every s. By (1b) with A := V (open, hence measurable) and hypothesis (iv):
 ∫_Ω h(s)·Dψ(s)(e_j) ds = ∫_Ω g(ι(s))·Df(ι(s))(τ_j) ds = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·Df(x)(τ_j) dH^n(x) = 0.
6. ((d) C¹ tests; supplied step 7, parenthetical remark.) By the accepted sibling smooth_to_c1_tests (dgcr_smooth_tests_to_C1_tests), applied with D := Ω (open, step 2), G := h (locally integrable on Ω, step 4) and the identities of step 5, ∫_{ℝ^n} h(s)·Dφ(s)(e_i) ds = 0 for every C¹ function φ with compact support, tsupport φ ⊆ Ω and every i. [Reason, as in the supplied step 7: the mollifications φ_ε of φ are C^∞, have supports in a fixed compact subset of Ω for small ε, and ∂_iφ_ε → ∂_iφ uniformly, while h is integrable on that compact set; so ∫ h∂_iφ = lim ∫ h∂_iφ_ε = 0.]
7. ((e) integrality and transfer back; supplied steps 7 and 8.) Let c₀ ∈ ℝ with h = c₀ L^n-a.e. on Ω. By (ii) and (1c) (with A := ℝ^P), h(s) ∈ ℤ for L^n-a.e. s ∈ ℝ^n. Ω is open and nonempty (step 3), so L^n(Ω) > 0 (IsOpen.measure_pos); hence some s ∈ Ω satisfies both h(s) = c₀ and h(s) = m for an integer m (Measure.exists_mem_of_measure_ne_zero_of_ae). Put c := m ∈ ℤ; then c₀ = c, and g(ι(s)) = h(s) = c for L^n-a.e. s ∈ Ω = ι^{−1}(V). By (1a) and (1c) with A := V, g(x) = c for H^n⌞(V ∩ Q)-a.e. x, i.e. for H^n-a.e. x ∈ V ∩ Q. ∎

subproblem.title: Signed integer density of an integer multiplicity current supported in an n-plane
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) an orthonormal family in ℝ^P, Q := span{τ_1, …, τ_n}, and S ∈ 𝒟_n(V) an integer multiplicity current (IsIntegerMultiplicity S) with spt S ⊆ Q. Then there is g : ℝ^P → ℝ such that, with H^n = μHE[n] and |g(x)| read as the extended norm ‖g x‖ₑ ∈ [0, ∞]: (i) g is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞Q; (ii) g(x) ∈ ℤ for H^n⌞Q-a.e. x; (iii) ∫_{K∩Q} |g| dH^n < ∞ (lower Lebesgue integral) for every compact K ⊆ V; (iv) S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)·ω(x)(τ_1, …, τ_n) dH^n(x) (Bochner integral) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V); (v) M_W(S) = S.massOn W = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n for every open W ⊆ V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (V : Set (Euclid P)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn V n) (τ : Fin n → Euclid P), IsOpen V → Orthonormal ℝ τ → IsIntegerMultiplicity S → S.support ⊆ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)) → ∃ g : Euclid P → ℝ, AEStronglyMeasurable g (μHE[n].restrict (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))) ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P))), ∃ m : ℤ, g x = m) ∧ (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ V → ∫⁻ x in K ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), ‖g x‖ₑ ∂μHE[n] ≠ ∞) ∧ (∀ ω : TestFormOn V n, S ω = ∫ x in V ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), g x * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x τ ∂μHE[n]) ∧ ∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → W ⊆ V → S.massOn W = ∫⁻ x in W ∩ (Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) : Set (Euclid P)), ‖g x‖ₑ ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 of the parent-supplied proof (Simon Ch. 6, 3.1–3.2 and the proof of the Constancy Theorem 2.34): the representation S = τ(M, θ, ξ), the carrier lying in Q, the orientation ±ξ_Q, and the signed integer density g := 1_M·ε·θ with μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q). Notation: H^n := μHE[n]; for an n-covector α, α(τ) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n); |g(x)| := ‖g x‖ₑ; 1_A is the indicator function of A.
1. (Representation.) Since S is integer multiplicity, choose R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep V n with R.Represents S. Thus M ⊆ V is Borel, θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable with θ ≥ 1 on M, ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ V (field locallyIntegrable_mult), ξ is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M, and S(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V). Let μ := R.measure = (H^n⌞M).withDensity θ.
2. (Mass, supplied step 1.) By the accepted sibling dimred_im_mass_measure (part (a); V is open and R represents S), M_W(S) = μ(W) for every open W ⊆ V.
3. (Carrier in the plane, supplied step 2.) H^n(M ∖ Q) = 0. Indeed, by the accepted sibling imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (V open, R represents S), H^n(M ∖ spt S) = 0, and M ∖ Q ⊆ M ∖ spt S because spt S ⊆ Q. [Equivalently, by the supplied argument: every x ∈ V ∖ Q lies outside spt S, so by dimred_im_mass_measure (b) it has a ball of μ-measure 0; by Lindelöf countably many such balls cover V ∖ Q, so μ(V ∖ Q) = 0, and H^n(M ∖ Q) ≤ μ(M ∖ Q) ≤ μ(V ∖ Q) = 0 because θ ≥ 1 on M ⊆ V.]
4. (Orientation, supplied step 4.) By the sibling child planar_orientation_sign (idtp_pc_orient_ae_eq_or_neg) applied to R, τ and step 3: for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α. Call such points x good. As M is measurable, the set of x ∈ M that are not good is H^n-null; equivalently, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P, x ∈ M implies that x is good (ae_restrict_iff').
5. (Sign function.) Fix an n-covector β₀ with β₀(τ) = 1: let δ be the determinant n-form of ℝ^n (δ(c_1, …, c_n) = det of the matrix with columns c_j; continuous, n-linear and alternating; δ(e_1, …, e_n) = 1), let ι* : ℝ^P → ℝ^n, ι*(y) := (⟨τ_1, y⟩, …, ⟨τ_n, y⟩) (continuous linear), and put β₀(w_1, …, w_n) := δ(ι*w_1, …, ι*w_n), i.e. β₀(w) = det(⟨τ_i, w_j⟩)_{i,j}; then β₀(τ) = δ(e_1, …, e_n) = 1 because ι*(τ_j) = e_j by orthonormality (for n = 0, β₀ is the constant 1). Put ε(x) := ξ(x)(β₀). Then ε is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M (composition of ξ with the continuous linear evaluation at β₀), and at every good x: ε(x) = ±β₀(τ) = ±1, ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}, and ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)·α(τ) for every n-covector α.
6. (Definition of g, supplied step 5.) Let g := 1_M·θ·ε, i.e. g(x) = θ(x)ε(x) for x ∈ M and g(x) = 0 for x ∉ M. By steps 4 and 5, for H^n-a.e. x ∈ ℝ^P: (a) g(x) ∈ ℤ (g(x) = ±θ(x) at good points of M, g(x) = 0 off M); (b) |g(x)| = 1_M(x)θ(x); (c) if x ∈ M then θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = g(x)α(τ) for every α.
7. ((i)–(iii).) (i): θ is measurable and ε is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M, so θε is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n⌞M; as M is measurable, its extension by 0, which is g, is a.e.-strongly measurable for H^n (aestronglyMeasurable_indicator_iff), hence for H^n⌞Q. (ii): 6(a) holds H^n-a.e., hence H^n⌞Q-a.e. (iii): for compact K ⊆ V, by 6(b), ∫_{K∩Q} |g| dH^n ≤ ∫_K |g| dH^n = ∫_K 1_M θ dH^n = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH^n < ∞ (step 1).
8. ((iv), the current identity.) Let ω ∈ 𝒟^n(V) and F(x) := g(x)·ω(x)(τ). By step 1, S(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^P} 1_M θ ξ(ω) dH^n, and ∫_{V∩Q} F dH^n = ∫_{ℝ^P} 1_{V∩Q} F dH^n. The two integrands agree H^n-a.e.: at H^n-a.e. x ∈ M we have x ∈ Q (step 3) and x ∈ V (M ⊆ V), so both equal θ(x)ξ(x)(ω(x)) = g(x)ω(x)(τ) by 6(c); at x ∉ M the first is 0 and the second is 0 as well, since g(x) = 0. Functions that agree a.e. have the same Bochner integral (no integrability is needed for this), so S(ω) = ∫_{V∩Q} g(x)ω(x)(τ) dH^n(x).
9. ((v), the mass identity; supplied step 5's μ = |g|·H^n⌞(V ∩ Q).) Let W ⊆ V be open. By step 2 and the definition of μ, M_W(S) = μ(W) = ∫_W θ d(H^n⌞M) = ∫_{W∩M} θ dH^n = ∫_W 1_M θ dH^n (withDensity_apply, W measurable; Measure.restrict_restrict; lintegral_indicator). By 6(b), ∫_W 1_M θ dH^n = ∫_W |g| dH^n. Finally |g| = 0 H^n-a.e. on W ∖ Q (g = 0 off M, and M ∖ Q is H^n-null by step 3), so ∫_W |g| dH^n = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n + ∫_{W∖Q} |g| dH^n = ∫_{W∩Q} |g| dH^n (lintegral_inter_add_sdiff with Q measurable).
